warnings.warning: Eq.3 tends to 1/d_i as R grows, while Table 1 calls d_i the upper limit, reversing the stated parameter role.
Eq.4 defines one rain-event timing density but supplies no annual event-count distribution in the baseline model.
Eq.6 omits plant count n_i even though Eq.19 and Eq.21 later multiply per-plant uptake by abundance.
Eq.12 initializes next-year biomass from the seed bank without visibly depleting the germinated seed stock.
Eq.13, Eq.21, and Eq.22 do not keep the sigma_ij versus sigma_ji direction consistent.
Eq.14 states only lambda_1+lambda_2=1 and omits the mapping from water-use capacities to the normalized weights.
Eq.15 and the later overlap equations do not implement the prose-required zero clamp when estimated overlap is negative.
Eq.19 uses c_i R-m_i while Eq.13 and Eq.21 use c_i f_i(R)-m_i, changing the growth mechanism without explanation.
Eq.13, Eq.21, and Eq.22 do not keep the sigma_ij versus sigma_ji direction consistent.
Eq.24 contains e^(1/R) although R is listed in kg; the exponent is dimensional, the no-shrub case does not return Eq.23's baseline, and the relative shrub effect is independent of R.
The claimed 95 percent interval uses plus/minus three sigma; a normal three-sigma interval is about 99.73 percent.
Over 10,000 square meters, 32.5 mm water has mass 325,000 kg, not 325 kg; all three reported masses are low by a factor of 1000.
Annual precipitation totals are used to calibrate Eq.5's per-event rainfall amount without a count or allocation model.
For lognormal rainfall E[exp(zeta)]=exp(mu+sigma^2/2), not exp(mu), so the stated mean mapping is wrong.
Eq.27-Eq.30 assume complete equal-edge binary trees, straight radial roots, half-sphere volume, and a universal beta from two taxa without uncertainty.
RK4 accuracy is conditional on step size and smoothness, yet no step, event localization, convergence, stiffness, or positivity control is reported.
The TOPSIS normalization, cost-direction conversion, weights, ideal points, distances, and closeness formula are omitted.
Figure 7 first crosses the one-species score at eight species, while page 17 says more than eight and the Summary says at least eight.
The shrub comparison uses four species versus three, confounding shrub facilitation with richness, composition, and initial-total differences.
The severe-drought scenario changes event count, amount center, and amount spread together and reports no ensemble or matched randomness.
Eq.35 leaves the uniform support unstated; the displayed variance corresponds to plus/minus five percent when 0.1 times the state is the total width, not plus/minus ten percent.
Eq.36-Eq.37 freeze water and dynamic sigma, omit impulses, seeds, death, and facilitation, and give positivity rather than Jacobian stability conditions.

main_argument_chains.claim: The shrub extension uses hydraulic-lift literature to modify herbaceous uptake and produces a shrub-versus-no-shrub scale-stability comparison.
